title: Qixian, Shanxi: A Buyer’s Guide to China’s Hand-Blown Glassware Capital
excerpt: Qixian County in Shanxi produces over 60% of China’s hand-blown glassware and exports more than 70% of it to 80+ countries. Here is what that means for importers.
body:
**Short answer:** Qixian County (祁县) in Jinzhong, Shanxi Province, is China’s core production area for hand-blown glassware. It accounts for more than 60% of national hand-blown output, and over 70% of its products are exported to more than 80 countries and regions, according to a February 2026 Xinhua report.

## Key facts about the Qixian glassware cluster

| Fact | Figure | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Share of China’s hand-blown glassware output | over 60% | Xinhua, Feb 2026 |
| Share of output exported | over 70% | Xinhua, Feb 2026 |
| Export destinations | 80+ countries and regions | Xinhua, Feb 2026 |
| Glassware manufacturers | 62, plus 230+ upstream/downstream firms | Xinhua, Feb 2026 |
| Local workers in glass-blowing | about 30,000 | Xinhua, Feb 2026 |
| Quality infrastructure | national-level glassware quality inspection center | Xinhua, Feb 2026 |

## How the industry started
Local historians trace the craft to Shanxi merchants who traded along the Ming–Qing "tea road" across Eurasia and brought glass-blowing techniques back home. More than a century later the county has a full supply chain: raw materials, molds, furnaces, decoration, packaging and export logistics.

## What Qixian is good at
- **Hand-blown stemware and decanters**: thin rims, pulled stems and complex shapes that machines cannot make economically
- **Colored and decorative glass**: ombre, overlay, patterned stems, gold decoration, styles popular in Europe and the Middle East
- **Small-batch flexibility**: hand production allows lower MOQs and faster design changes than fully automated plants
- **Borosilicate**: newer automated lines now produce heat-resistant glassware at scale

## What to check before you order
1. **Process match**: hand-blown, mold-blown or machine-pressed? Each factory specializes.
2. **Glass type**: soda-lime, lead-free crystal or borosilicate, which affects clarity, weight and price.
3. **Tolerance**: hand-made items vary slightly; agree on acceptable ranges for height, weight and capacity.
4. **Packaging**: glass needs drop-tested export cartons; confirm this in the quotation.
5. **Inspection**: insist on pre-shipment QC with photos.

## Why work with a local sourcing partner
With dozens of factories each focusing on different processes, the fastest route is a local team that already knows which workshop makes which product well. We visit the factories, compare quotations, follow production and inspect goods before they leave Shanxi.

*Source: Xinhua, "Glass-blowing craft thrives in China's ancient county", 21 Feb 2026.*

title: Hand-Blown vs Machine-Made Glassware: Which Is Right for Your Market?
excerpt: Choose hand-blown glass for premium, thin-rim or small-batch designs; choose machine-made for high volume, consistent sizes and lower unit cost.
body:
**Short answer:** Hand-blown glassware suits premium positioning, thin rims, unusual shapes and small batches. Machine-made glassware suits high volumes, tight size consistency and the lowest unit cost.

## Side-by-side comparison

| Factor | Hand-blown | Machine-made |
|---|---|---|
| Typical MOQ | 300–1,000 pcs | 3,000–10,000+ pcs |
| Unit cost | Higher | Lower |
| Rim | Can be very thin (≈1 mm), cut and polished | Usually thicker, rolled or fire-polished |
| Size consistency | Small variations | Very consistent |
| Design flexibility | High, quick changes | Needs molds; changes cost more |
| Lead time | 35–50 days | 25–40 days |
| Best for | Wine brands, premium retail, decor | Supermarkets, hotels, promotions |

## When to choose hand-blown
- You sell on look and feel: crystal stemware, decanters, art vases
- You need colored, ombre or overlay effects
- You want to test a new collection without a large commitment

## When to choose machine-made
- You need 10,000+ identical pieces for chain stores or hospitality
- Stackability and exact capacity matter
- Price is the main purchase driver

## A mixed approach
Many buyers combine both: a machine-made core range for volume, plus hand-blown hero items for margin and brand image. We can source both from Shanxi and consolidate them into one shipment.

title: Borosilicate vs Soda-Lime vs Lead-Free Crystal: A Glass Material Guide for Importers
excerpt: Soda-lime is the low-cost everyday glass; borosilicate resists heat and thermal shock; lead-free crystal gives the best clarity and brilliance for stemware.
body:
**Short answer:** Use **soda-lime glass** for everyday tumblers and jars, **borosilicate glass** for hot drinks and cookware, and **lead-free crystal** for premium wine glasses and decanters.

## Comparison

| Property | Soda-lime | Borosilicate 3.3 | Lead-free crystal |
|---|---|---|---|
| Main use | Tumblers, jars, vases | Teapots, mugs, storage, labware | Wine glasses, decanters, barware |
| Heat resistance | Low; avoid boiling water shocks | High (thermal shock ΔT ≈ 120 °C+) | Low–medium |
| Clarity and brilliance | Good | Good, slightly lighter feel | Excellent, higher refractive index |
| Weight | Medium | Light | Medium |
| Relative cost | $ | $$ | $$–$$$ |

## Soda-lime glass
Soda-lime is the most widely manufactured type of glass. It is inexpensive, recyclable and easy to color. It is not designed for sudden temperature changes.

## Borosilicate glass
Boron oxide lowers thermal expansion, so borosilicate tolerates hot liquids and temperature changes. It is the right choice for teapots, double-wall cups, coffee carafes and oven-safe containers.

## Lead-free crystal
Modern crystal replaces lead oxide with barium, zinc or titanium oxides. It gives high clarity, a fine ring and allows very thin rims. It is the preferred material for premium stemware.

## Compliance tips
- Ask for **food-contact test reports** (FDA for the US, LFGB for Germany, EU 1935/2004 for the EU)
- For decorated glass, test the **lip and rim area** for lead and cadmium release
- Specify the glass type in the purchase contract

title: How to Choose a Glass Perfume Bottle Supplier in China: A 10-Point Checklist
excerpt: Check five things before you pay a deposit: the neck finish fits your pump, the factory owns the mold, samples match production, decoration is done in-house or by a trusted partner, and packing is drop-tested.
body:
**Short answer:** A good perfume bottle supplier can show you the exact mold in stock, confirm the neck finish fits your pump, send production-grade samples, and explain who does each decoration step. If a supplier cannot answer these clearly, keep looking.

## The 10-point checklist

| # | What to check | Why it matters | What to ask for |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Mold ownership** | Stock molds are cheaper and faster; a new mold adds cost and 2–4 weeks | Photo or video of the bottle from the existing mold |
| 2 | **Neck finish** | A mismatch between bottle and pump is the most common perfume packaging failure | Neck drawing with size (e.g. 15 mm crimp / FEA 15) |
| 3 | **Glass weight and base thickness** | Heavy bases feel premium but affect cost and shipping weight | Weight in grams and a cross-section photo |
| 4 | **Capacity tolerance** | Brim-full and fill-level volumes differ | Brim capacity and recommended fill level |
| 5 | **Decoration route** | Spray coating, frosting, printing and hot stamping are often done by separate workshops | Who does each step, and where |
| 6 | **Color matching** | Spray colors shift between batches without a standard | Pantone reference and an approved color sample |
| 7 | **Closures as a set** | Bottle, pump, collar and cap from different vendors may not fit | A tested set: bottle + pump + collar + cap |
| 8 | **Quality standard** | Bubbles, stones, uneven bases and scratches are normal defects to control | AQL level and a defect list with photos |
| 9 | **Packing** | Heavy glass bottles break if cartons are weak | Inner dividers, carton strength, drop test |
| 10 | **Lead time** | Decoration and cap production often take longer than the glass itself | A schedule for each component |

## Red flags
- The "factory" cannot show the production line or the mold, only catalog photos
- Very low prices with no mention of the neck finish or glass weight
- No sample policy, or samples that differ from the quoted specification
- Decoration quoted without color approval

## How Shanxi fits in
Shanxi Province, especially the Qixian glass cluster, has decades of experience in glass forming, polishing and hand-finishing. Many perfume bottle factories in the region combine heavy-base flint glass with decoration such as [air-bubble effects](/products/perfume-bottles/air-bubble-glass-perfume-bottle-90-ml), [polished facets](/products/perfume-bottles/polished-faceted-glass-perfume-bottle-100-ml) and [spray-coated gradients](/products/perfume-bottles/spray-coated-gradient-perfume-bottle-100-ml).

## Next step
Send us your target capacity, neck finish (or pump model), quantity and reference photos. We will shortlist matching stock molds from vetted Shanxi factories and arrange samples. Browse our [glass perfume bottles](/products/perfume-bottles) or [request a quote](/contact).

title: Perfume Bottle Neck Finishes Explained: FEA 15 Crimp vs Screw Neck
excerpt: Crimp necks such as FEA 15 give the cleanest, most leak-resistant seal but need a crimping tool; screw necks are easier for small batches and refills. Always choose the pump and the bottle together.
body:
**Short answer:** Most fine-fragrance bottles use a **crimp neck**, most often **15 mm (FEA 15)**. The pump is crimped permanently onto the glass, which gives a clean look and a reliable seal. **Screw necks** (for example 18/415) let you close bottles by hand and allow refilling, which suits small batches, samples and refillable concepts.

## The main options

| Neck type | How the pump is fixed | Pros | Cons | Typical use |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Crimp (e.g. FEA 13, 15, 18, 20)** | Metal ferrule of the pump is crimped around the glass neck | Slim, premium look; strong seal; collar hides the joint | Needs a crimping tool; not refillable | Eau de parfum, eau de toilette |
| **Screw neck (e.g. 18/415, 20/410)** | Pump screws onto a threaded neck | No machine needed; refillable; easy for small runs | Visible thread or bulkier collar | Samples, body mists, refillable lines |
| **Snap-on (no-crimp)** | Pump presses onto the neck | Fast filling without crimping | Fewer pump choices; check seal carefully | Mid-range and gift sets |

FEA is the code system used by the European perfume packaging industry for crimp neck sizes. The number refers to the neck diameter in millimetres.

## How to avoid fit problems
1. **Pick the pump and bottle together.** Ask the supplier to test the exact pump on the exact bottle.
2. **Check the dip tube length.** It must reach the bottom corner of the bottle. Heavy-base bottles have a raised inner bottom, so the tube is often shorter than you expect.
3. **Test the collar.** Decorative collars must sit flush on the shoulder and leave room for the cap.
4. **Approve a full set.** Approve bottle + pump + collar + cap together, then keep one set as the golden sample.

## Crimping in practice
Small brands can use a manual crimping tool for a few hundred bottles. For larger volumes, filling companies use pneumatic crimpers. Tell us how you plan to fill, and we will suggest the right neck.

Most bottles in our [perfume bottle range](/products/perfume-bottles) use a 15 mm crimp neck, for example the [clear heavy-base 100 ml bottle](/products/perfume-bottles/clear-heavy-base-glass-perfume-bottle-100-ml). Screw-neck versions are available on request. [Ask for a fitted sample set](/contact).

title: Custom Perfume Bottle Cost and MOQ: What Really Drives the Price
excerpt: The unit price of a perfume bottle is driven mainly by glass weight, whether a stock mold exists, decoration steps and the cap. Using a stock mold with your own color and logo is the fastest way to a low MOQ.
body:
**Short answer:** The biggest cost drivers are **(1) stock mold or new mold, (2) glass weight, (3) number of decoration steps, and (4) the cap**. If you start from a stock mold and customize the color, logo and cap, MOQs are usually in the low thousands and lead times stay around 30–45 days.

## Cost drivers, from biggest to smallest

| Driver | Effect on price | How to save |
|---|---|---|
| **New mold** | One-time mold fee plus 2–4 extra weeks | Start from a stock mold; customize it with decoration |
| **Glass weight** | Heavier bottles use more glass and cost more to ship | Choose the lightest base that still looks premium |
| **Decoration steps** | Each step (frosting, spray, printing, hot stamping) adds cost and some loss | Combine effects: e.g. a gradient spray plus one-color print |
| **Cap** | Zinc alloy and heavy acrylic caps can cost as much as the bottle | Surlyn or ABS caps with metallic finish |
| **Quantity** | Set-up costs are shared across the order | Group several sizes from one mold family |
| **Quality level** | Tighter defect limits mean more rejects | Agree on an AQL that matches your retail channel |

## Typical MOQ ranges
These are common starting points with Shanxi factories; the exact figure depends on the mold and decoration.

| Option | Typical MOQ |
|---|---|
| Stock mold, clear | about 3,000–5,000 pcs |
| Stock mold + spray color or print | about 3,000 pcs per color |
| Hot-fused or polished designs | about 2,000–3,000 pcs |
| Hand-made bottles | from about 500 pcs per design |
| New mold | usually 10,000 pcs or more to justify the mold |

## Lead time
- Stock bottles: about 20–30 days
- Decorated bottles: about 30–45 days
- New mold: add 2–4 weeks for mold making and samples

Caps and pumps are often the slowest part, so order them at the same time as the glass.

## How to get an accurate quote
Send capacity, target glass weight, neck finish, decoration, cap type, quantity per design, and destination. With that, we can quote stock-mold options from our [perfume bottle range](/products/perfume-bottles) within 1–3 working days. [Request a quote](/contact).

title: Glass Skincare Packaging Guide: Dropper Bottles, Pump Bottles and Cream Jars
excerpt: Use dropper bottles for oils and serums, pump bottles for lotions and emulsions, and wide jars for thick creams. Pick the glass color for your formula, and order the whole series from one supplier so finishes match.
body:
**Short answer:** Match the pack to the texture: **dropper bottles** for oils and thin serums, **pump bottles** for lotions and emulsions, and **jars** for thick creams and balms. For light-sensitive formulas, choose amber or fully coated glass. Order the whole series from one supplier so the color and finish match across sizes.

## Which pack for which product

| Product texture | Best pack | Typical sizes | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Facial oil, thin serum | Dropper bottle | 15–50 ml | Glass pipette doses precisely; check bulb material against your oils |
| Essence, toner | Bottle with orifice reducer or fine mist | 100–200 ml | Mist sprayers give a lighter application |
| Lotion, emulsion | Pump bottle | 30–120 ml | Treatment pumps for 0.2 ml doses; lotion pumps for larger doses |
| Cream, balm, mask | Wide-mouth jar | 15–100 g | Inner liner protects the formula and the cap |

## Glass finishes
- **Clear**: shows the product; best for stable, colorful formulas
- **Frosted**: soft, premium look; made by acid etching or spray
- **Solid or gradient color**: full brand color via spray coating, matched to Pantone
- **Pearlescent or electroplated**: metallic shine for prestige lines
- **Amber**: filters much of the light that can degrade sensitive ingredients

## Planning a full series
A launch usually needs a cleanser or toner, a serum, a lotion and a cream. Choosing one series from one supplier keeps the shoulder shape, glass color and cap finish consistent. See our [skincare glass packaging set](/products/skincare-cosmetic-bottles/skincare-glass-packaging-set-toner-lotion-cream).

## Compatibility tests to run
1. **Fill and leak test** with your actual formula, upside down for 24–48 hours
2. **Dose test** for pumps and droppers
3. **Decoration rub test** with your formula on the outside of the bottle
4. **Drop test** of the packed retail box

- [Gradient lotion pump bottle 100 ml](/products/skincare-cosmetic-bottles/gradient-glass-lotion-pump-bottle-100-ml)
- [Thick-wall cream jar 50 g](/products/skincare-cosmetic-bottles/thick-wall-glass-cream-jar-50-g)

Tell us your formulas and sizes and we will suggest a matching series. [Request samples](/contact).

title: Is Soda-Lime Glass Lead-Free? What Buyers of Decorated Glassware Should Check
excerpt: Soda-lime glass is made without lead. Decorated glassware is different: paints, enamels and decals need their own testing. Here is what to ask for.
body:
**Short answer:** Yes. Soda-lime glass is made without lead, so the glass itself is lead-free. Decorated soda-lime glassware is a different question. Paints, enamels, decals and gold rims are separate materials, and they need their own testing. If you are buying hand-painted or printed drinkware, ask for a test report on the decorated product, not only on the plain glass.

## What soda-lime glass is made of

Soda-lime glass is the most common glass in the world. It is used for drinking glasses, bottles, jars and windows. Its recipe is simple:

| Ingredient | Typical share | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| Silica (sand) | about 70–74% | Forms the glass |
| Soda (sodium oxide) | about 12–16% | Lowers the melting temperature |
| Lime (calcium oxide) | about 5–12% | Makes the glass stable and durable |
| Small additions (magnesium, aluminium oxides) | a few percent | Adjust strength and working properties |

Lead is not part of this recipe. That is why plain soda-lime tumblers, highballs and rocks glasses are described as lead-free.

## How it differs from crystal

The confusion usually comes from crystal. Traditional lead crystal is made with lead oxide, typically 24% or more, which gives it extra sparkle, weight and a ringing sound. “Lead-free crystal” replaces the lead with other oxides such as barium, zinc, potassium or titanium.

| Glass type | Contains lead in the recipe? | Typical use |
|---|---|---|
| Soda-lime glass | No | Everyday drinkware, jars, bottles |
| Borosilicate glass | No | Teaware, coffee cups, heat-resistant glass |
| Lead-free crystal | No | Premium stemware and decanters |
| Lead crystal | Yes | Traditional cut crystal |

Our guide to [borosilicate vs soda-lime vs lead-free crystal](/blog/borosilicate-vs-soda-lime-vs-crystal-glass) compares the materials in more detail.

## Where lead can appear on decorated glassware

On decorated glassware, the risk is in the decoration, not the glass. Colored enamels, some paints, decals and metallic rims can contain lead or cadmium, depending on the pigments the decorator uses. This matters most where the decoration touches food or the drinker’s mouth.

- **The lip-and-rim area.** This is the band at the top of a drinking glass, usually the top 20 mm, where the lips touch. In the US, externally decorated tumblers are commonly tested with **ASTM C927**, a method that measures lead and cadmium extracted from the lip-and-rim area.
- **Food-contact surfaces.** Bowls, plates and the inside of glasses can be tested for lead and cadmium release under the rules of your market, such as US FDA requirements, the EU framework regulation (EC) No 1935/2004, or German LFGB.
- **California.** Products sold in California must meet Proposition 65 requirements. Many US retailers apply Prop 65 limits to all their glassware, wherever it is sold.

A design with decoration kept away from the rim, such as our [Colorful Swirl Base Rocks Glass (RCK-SWL-001)](/products/tumblers-drinking-glasses/colorful-swirl-base-rocks-glass) or [Multicolor Base Tumbler (TMB-BAS-001)](/products/tumblers-drinking-glasses/multicolor-base-tumbler), has a lower lip-and-rim risk. Designs painted all the way to the top, such as mosaic tumblers, should be tested on the rim area.

## How to check a supplier’s claim

“Lead-free” on a product page or a quotation is a claim, not proof. Before you launch a decorated glassware range, ask for:

1. **A test report on the decorated item.** A report on undecorated glass does not cover the paint.
2. **A report from an accredited laboratory.** Look for a lab accredited to ISO/IEC 17025 for the test method.
3. **A matching item code and photo.** The report should name the product you are buying, with the same decoration and colors.
4. **The right method for your market.** For example, ASTM C927 for US lip-and-rim testing, and food-contact testing for your destination.
5. **A recent date.** Ask for a new test if the factory changes its paint, enamel or decal supplier.

If a report does not exist yet, plan the test into your sampling time. Testing is usually done on approved production samples, so it can run in parallel with your packaging approval.

## What we do

Our glassware is made from soda-lime, borosilicate or lead-free crystal glass. For decorated items, we tell you which reports are available for each item code, and we arrange testing at an accredited lab when your market needs it. We do not describe a decorated product as tested unless a report covers it.

Browse our [hand-painted glassware collection](/collections/hand-painted-glassware), or read the [hand-painted glassware buyer’s guide](/blog/hand-painted-glassware-wholesale-buyers-guide) for sampling, MOQ and packaging. To ask about testing for a specific item, [send us an inquiry](/contact) with the item code and your target market.

title: Hand-Painted Glassware Wholesale: A Buyer’s Guide to Samples, MOQ and Packaging
excerpt: How to buy hand-painted glassware wholesale: approved samples, acceptable variation, MOQ per design and color, packaging, testing and range planning.
body:
**Short answer:** To buy hand-painted glassware wholesale, start from an approved sample, agree how much variation between pieces is acceptable, and confirm MOQ per design and per color in the quotation. Plan packaging and testing at the same time as sampling, not after. Most problems with decorated glassware come from unclear samples, weak cartons or missing test reports, not from the painting itself.

## What “hand-painted” means in production

On hand-painted glassware, workers apply the pattern by hand onto a finished glass blank. The blank may be pressed or blown, and it is often a stock shape with a molded texture, such as a cut-diamond or ribbed surface that guides the paint.

Two things are worth asking about:

- **How the pattern is placed.** Some designs are painted freehand. Others follow molded lines or stencils, which gives a more regular result.
- **How the paint is cured.** Some decorations use glass paints cured at a lower temperature. Others use glass enamels fired at a higher temperature, which bond more strongly to the glass. The method affects durability, dishwasher resistance and testing. Our guide on [whether hand-painted glasses are dishwasher safe](/blog/are-hand-painted-glasses-dishwasher-safe) explains the difference.

## Agree what “consistent” means

Hand painting means no two pieces are identical. Retail buyers usually accept this, as long as the overall look matches the sample. Before production, agree on:

1. **An approved sample** kept by you and by the factory, labeled with the item code.
2. **Acceptable variation.** For example: color shades, line thickness, small gaps, or paint on the base.
3. **Defects.** For example: paint runs, missed areas, scratches, bubbles or chips in the glass.
4. **How pieces are inspected.** A pre-shipment inspection checks a random sample of each lot against the approved sample, using an AQL sampling plan.

Clear photos of acceptable and unacceptable pieces make inspection faster and avoid disputes later.

## What drives MOQ

MOQ for hand-painted glassware depends on more than the glass blank. Ask for MOQ in this order:

| Factor | Why it matters |
|---|---|
| Per design | Each pattern needs set-up and trained painters |
| Per color combination | New colors need new paint batches and approval |
| Glass blank | Stock blanks have lower MOQs than new molds |
| Packaging | Printed gift boxes have their own MOQ, often higher than the glass |
| Mixed cartons | Mixing designs in one carton may change carton MOQ |

If your first order is small, keep the stock color combination and use plain or stock packaging. Custom colors and printed boxes work better on repeat orders.

## Sampling and timeline

A typical project runs in this order:

1. **Existing samples** of stock designs, usually within days.
2. **Custom samples** with your colors or layout, usually one to two weeks.
3. **Approval** of the sample, packaging and carton marks.
4. **Testing** on approved samples if your market requires it. Read [is soda-lime glass lead-free?](/blog/is-soda-lime-glass-lead-free) for what to test on decorated drinkware.
5. **Production and inspection**, then shipping.

Hand painting is slower than machine decoration, so production time depends on the design and order size. Lead time is confirmed in each quotation. For holiday ranges, work back from your in-store date with our [holiday glassware sourcing calendar](/blog/holiday-glassware-sourcing-calendar).

## Packaging and breakage

Glass breaks in transit when cartons are weak or pieces touch. For decorated glassware, also protect the paint from scratching.

- Use **inner boxes or dividers** so pieces do not touch.
- Ask for **carton drop testing**. ISTA test procedures are common for retail shipments.
- Confirm **carton size, gross weight and pieces per carton** before you plan a container.
- For gift sets, approve the box insert with the actual glass, not a drawing.

## Build a range, not a list of items

Retail buyers sell more when designs work together on the shelf. When you choose designs:

- Pick **two heights** in the same pattern, such as the [Multicolor Mosaic Tumbler (TMB-MOS-001)](/products/tumblers-drinking-glasses/multicolor-mosaic-tumbler) and the [Multicolor Mosaic Highball (HBG-MOS-002)](/products/tumblers-drinking-glasses/multicolor-mosaic-highball).
- Add a **matching bowl or plate**, such as the [mosaic glass bowl](/products/glass-bowls-plates/multicolor-mosaic-glass-bowl) and [mosaic rim plate](/products/glass-bowls-plates/mosaic-rim-glass-plate).
- Balance **year-round designs** with **gift and seasonal designs**. Our collections follow this split: [hand-painted glassware](/collections/hand-painted-glassware), [floral and gift glassware](/collections/floral-gift-glassware), [holiday glassware](/collections/holiday-glassware) and [bar and restaurant glassware](/collections/bar-restaurant-glassware).

## Questions to ask any supplier

- Is the decoration painted freehand or along molded lines?
- Is the paint cured at low temperature or fired as an enamel?
- What is the MOQ per design and per color?
- Which test reports exist for this item code, and from which lab?
- What is the recommended care instruction for the label?
- How many pieces per carton, and has the carton been drop tested?

When you are ready, [send us an inquiry](/contact) with the item codes, quantity per design, target market and packaging needs. We confirm MOQ, lead time, packaging and price in the quotation.

title: Holiday Glassware Sourcing Calendar: When to Order Halloween and Christmas Glassware
excerpt: US Halloween and Christmas glassware orders are usually confirmed 6 to 9 months ahead. A month-by-month calendar for importing seasonal glassware from China.
body:
**Short answer:** For US retail, Halloween and Christmas glassware orders are usually confirmed 6 to 9 months before the holiday. That means sampling Halloween designs in January and February, and placing orders by spring. Chinese New Year pauses most factories for several weeks in January or February, so samples should be approved before the break.

The dates below are typical planning windows for buyers importing from China. Your own retailer calendar comes first, so use this as a starting point and confirm dates with your buying team.

## Why holiday glassware needs early orders

Seasonal glassware has a short selling window. A Halloween glass that arrives after mid-September loses most of its season. Four steps take time:

- **Sampling and approval:** new colors, motifs and gift boxes need samples, and you may need test reports for decorated drinkware.
- **Production:** hand-painted and decorated items take longer than plain glass.
- **Ocean freight:** roughly 2 to 3 weeks from China to the US West Coast and 4 to 6 weeks to the East Coast, port to port, before customs and inland delivery.
- **Distribution:** goods move from the port to your warehouse and then to stores.

## Typical calendar for the US market

| Season | In stores | Leave China | Production | Confirm order | Sample and approve |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Valentine’s Day | early January | October–November | August–October | July–August | May–July |
| Easter and spring | February–March | November–December | September–November | August–September | June–August |
| Mother’s Day | April | January | October–December | September–October | July–September |
| Fourth of July | May–June | February–March | December–February | November | September–October |
| Halloween and fall | late August–September | June–July | April–June | March–April | January–February |
| Christmas | October–November | August–September | May–August | April–May | February–March |

Two notes on this table:

- **Spring and summer ranges overlap Chinese New Year.** Mother’s Day goods usually need to ship before the factory break, and Fourth of July goods are often in production during it. Allow extra time for both.
- **Big retailers plan earlier.** Large chains often review seasonal ranges at trade shows and line reviews 9 to 12 months ahead. Smaller importers can often work closer to the 6-month mark.

## Plan around Chinese New Year

Chinese New Year is the biggest scheduling risk in the year. In 2027 it falls in early February. Most factories close for two to four weeks around the holiday, and production often runs slower for a few weeks afterwards while workers return.

To avoid delays:

1. Approve samples and packaging **before mid-January**.
2. Confirm orders early enough for the factory to buy materials before the break.
3. Expect a slower start in late February and March.

## Other seasons worth planning

- **Ramadan and Eid** move about 11 days earlier each year. Check the dates for your year and plan Middle East orders 4 to 6 months ahead. The [Gold Geometric Glass Plate (PLT-GLD-001)](/products/glass-bowls-plates/gold-geometric-glass-plate) suits these programs.
- **Thanksgiving** follows Halloween in the US, so autumn designs such as the [Pumpkin Glass Tumbler (TMB-PUM-001)](/products/tumblers-drinking-glasses/pumpkin-glass-tumbler) sell for longer than purely Halloween designs.

## Match designs to seasons

| Season | Designs |
|---|---|
| Halloween and fall | [Pumpkin Glass Tumbler](/products/tumblers-drinking-glasses/pumpkin-glass-tumbler), [Ghost Glass Tumbler](/products/tumblers-drinking-glasses/ghost-glass-tumbler) |
| Christmas | [Gingerbread Man Glass Tumbler](/products/tumblers-drinking-glasses/gingerbread-man-glass-tumbler), [Candy Cane Glass Tumbler](/products/tumblers-drinking-glasses/candy-cane-glass-tumbler), [Red Stem Dessert Bowl](/products/glass-bowls-plates/red-stem-dessert-bowl) |
| Valentine’s Day | [Heart Votive Holder](/products/candle-holders-jars/heart-votive-holder), [Heart Glass Cup](/products/tumblers-drinking-glasses/heart-glass-cup) |
| Spring and Mother’s Day | [Butterfly Pattern Tumbler](/products/tumblers-drinking-glasses/butterfly-pattern-tumbler), [Hand-Painted Tulip Vase](/products/glass-vases-home-decor/hand-painted-tulip-vase) |
| Fourth of July | [Red Blue Mosaic Highball](/products/tumblers-drinking-glasses/red-blue-mosaic-highball), [Stemmed Dessert Bowl](/products/glass-bowls-plates/stemmed-dessert-bowl) |

See all seasonal designs in our [holiday glassware collection](/collections/holiday-glassware), and gift designs in the [floral and gift glassware collection](/collections/floral-gift-glassware).

## Checklist before you confirm a seasonal order

- In-store date and the date goods must reach your warehouse
- Quantity per design, and whether designs ship mixed in one carton
- Gift box or retail pack, with artwork deadline
- Test reports needed for your market, such as lip-and-rim testing for decorated drinkware
- Carton data for container planning
- A shipping date that leaves time for delays

Read the [hand-painted glassware buyer’s guide](/blog/hand-painted-glassware-wholesale-buyers-guide) for sampling and packaging details. To plan a seasonal range, [send us an inquiry](/contact) with your season, quantity per design and in-store date. We confirm MOQ, lead time and packaging in the quotation.

title: Are Hand-Painted Glasses Dishwasher Safe? Decoration Methods and Testing Explained
excerpt: Whether hand-painted glasses survive a dishwasher depends on how the paint is applied and cured. How to test, and what to put on the care label.
body:
**Short answer:** Not always. It depends on how the paint is applied and cured. Glass enamels fired at high temperature bond to the glass and usually survive home dishwashers well. Paints cured at lower temperatures are more likely to fade or wear, so hand washing is often recommended. Before you print “dishwasher safe” on a label, ask for dishwasher resistance results on the actual item.

## Why hand-painted decoration wears in a dishwasher

Dishwashers are hard on decoration for four reasons:

- **Heat.** Wash and rinse water is hot, and commercial machines run hotter than home machines.
- **Alkaline detergent.** Dishwasher detergents are strongly alkaline and slowly attack paint and glass surfaces.
- **Abrasion.** Glasses rub against racks and other items during the cycle.
- **Repetition.** Damage builds up. A glass that looks fine after 10 washes may fade after 200.

Plain glass is affected too. Over many cycles, glass can develop a cloudy or rainbow film called glass corrosion or etching, especially with soft water and too much detergent. Decoration usually shows wear first.

## How the decoration method changes durability

| Decoration | How it is made | Typical durability |
|---|---|---|
| Fired glass enamel | Paint with glass particles, fired at high temperature to fuse with the surface | Most durable; often suitable for home dishwashers |
| Low-temperature glass paint | Paint cured in an oven at a lower temperature | Less durable; often hand wash recommended |
| Decal | Printed transfer applied to the glass, then fired or cured | Depends on whether it is fired |
| Applied glass motifs | Colored glass shapes attached to the outside | Depends on the attachment; raised parts can knock against racks |
| Colored glass | Color is part of the glass itself | As durable as the glass |

Ask your supplier which method each item uses. On our product pages, the specifications show the decoration type, such as hand-painted or raised glass appliqués. Ask us whether a painted design is fired or cured at low temperature, and we confirm it in the quotation.

## How dishwasher resistance is tested

Dishwasher resistance is tested by washing samples for a set number of cycles and comparing them with unwashed pieces. The **EN 12875** series of European standards covers mechanical dishwashing resistance of utensils, and many labs offer tests based on it. Retailers may also set their own cycle counts.

When you ask for a test, agree:

1. **Domestic or commercial conditions.** Commercial testing is harsher.
2. **Number of cycles.** More cycles give a more realistic picture of product life.
3. **Pass criteria.** For example: no visible fading, no peeling, no loss of gloss.
4. **The exact item.** Test the decorated item you are buying, in the final colors.

If you cannot wait for a lab, run a simple check on samples. Wash a few pieces daily in a home dishwasher, keep one unwashed piece as a control, and compare them under good light after a few weeks. This does not replace a lab report, but it shows weaknesses early.

## Home use vs restaurants and bars

For hotels, restaurants, bars and cafes, choose designs that keep the decoration away from the rim and the areas that rub most. Examples:

- [Colorful Swirl Base Rocks Glass (RCK-SWL-001)](/products/tumblers-drinking-glasses/colorful-swirl-base-rocks-glass): color is inside the base, with a clear rim and walls
- [Multicolor Base Tumbler (TMB-BAS-001)](/products/tumblers-drinking-glasses/multicolor-base-tumbler): color on the lower band only
- [Green Faceted Rocks Glass (RCK-GRN-001)](/products/tumblers-drinking-glasses/green-faceted-rocks-glass): color on the lower half

Fully painted designs, such as mosaic tumblers, suit retail and home use better. See the [bar and restaurant glassware collection](/collections/bar-restaurant-glassware) for hospitality designs.

## What to put on the care label

Until you have test results, the safe instruction for hand-painted glassware is:

> Hand wash recommended. Do not soak. Avoid abrasive sponges.

After testing, you can use the claim your results support, such as “top-rack dishwasher safe” for domestic use. Keep the test report on file in case a retailer asks for it.

## Related guides

- [Is soda-lime glass lead-free?](/blog/is-soda-lime-glass-lead-free) explains testing for decorated drinkware.
- The [hand-painted glassware buyer’s guide](/blog/hand-painted-glassware-wholesale-buyers-guide) covers samples, MOQ and packaging.

To ask about decoration methods and test results for a specific item, [send us an inquiry](/contact) with the item code and whether the glasses are for home or commercial use.
